This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. Amid renewed tensions with President Trump, Ukraine says the satellite communication system it uses for drone missions has been placed under restrictions.
Ukraine's military uses Star Shield, the military version of Elon Musk's Starlink. Here's NPR's Greg Myry.
Ukraine's defense ministry said in a statement that "without warning, the Star Shield terminals were unilaterally limited."
Ukraine says that when its drones exceed 100 miles per hour, which they routinely do, the communication link is cut with the drone operator.
So this is a huge blow to Ukraine if this restriction stays in effect.
Ukraine says it's in contact with the U.S. government and SpaceX to try to sort out the problem.
Elon Musk said on social media that the U.S. government controls Star Shield.
President Trump has been telling Ukraine to stop attacking Russian oil facilities.
Democratic and Republican Party leaders have been in a legal battle about ad raids since earlier this year, and the Supreme Court has again sided with Republicans, at least for now, NPR's Maham Javed reports.
The GOP has been given another win in the ongoing ad-rate dispute between the two parties.
A recent Federal Communications Commission policy gives party committees discounted ad rates previously only offered to candidates.
Democratic leaders, including former Senator Sherrod Brown, challenged this policy, and a lower court ordered the FCC to finalize its new rule before the November 3rd elections.
Now the Supreme Court has intervened, saying the FCC does not have to follow that deadline.
This means both party committees can continue to enjoy discounted ad rates for the upcoming midterm, and the Republican Party Committee has considerably more in its coffers than its Democratic counterpart, Maham Javed, NPR News.
The parent has filed a class action lawsuit against OpenAI for allowing her teenage children to use chat GPT without parental consent and profiting off their data, NPR's Ho Ching Don reports.
The lawsuit filed in California alleges that OpenAI allowed the plaintiff's children to bypass its parental consent requirement easily, and that the chatbot continued to engage with one of the children even after the girl said that she was 12, below the minimum user age that OpenAI laid out in its own policy.
According to the complaint, the children shared intimate life details with the chatbot, including selfies, their anxieties about their appearance, and a photo of insects in the bathroom.
The plaintiff alleges that OpenAI unjustly profits off of such user data and demands compensation from the company.
In response to NPR, OpenAI says it strongly disagrees with its "misguided lawsuit."
It says it requires parental consent for underage users and lets teen users opt out of letting OpenAI train on their data.
Ho Ching Don, NPR News.
In Northwestern Pakistan, rescuers are working to reach several children, reported trapped beneath the rubble of a roof collapse.
The collapse happened at a private school. Officials now say at least 27 children and a teacher were killed.
In Albania, protests in the capital have turned violent, with several arrests and Piers Rob Schmitz reports.
The student-led demonstrations have joined an ongoing anti-government movement known as the Flamingo Revolution, which is demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Eddie Rama over allegations of corruption.
Rama is a vocal supporter of a luxury coastal development project linked to Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump that protesters say will harm the fragile coastal environment in southern Albania.
This week, Tarana saw violent clashes between student protesters and police as demonstrators threw stones and smashed shop windows.
Police responded with tear gas and water cannons, arresting at least 23 people. Six police officers and one journalist were injured.
Rob Schmitz, NPR News, Washington.
Financial markets in Asia fell sharply in Thursday trading. South Korea's benchmark declined by more than 7 percent, and Japan's Nikkei slipped 4.5 percent amid a deepening sell-off in technology shares.
The losses in Asia follow Wednesday's declines on Wall Street after the government said inflation worsened in September.
I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR News.
